spans.title: Sigurd's Cavern
spans.blurb: Deep in a torchlit cavern, an English traveler meets its keeper, a misshapen dwarf with wild blue eyes who says the dead have summoned him across the sea.
spans.spoilerNote: Sigurd's prophecy hints early at the book's central romance and foreshadows how his own devotion to Thelma will end.

spans.title: The Worst Dancer at Court
spans.blurb: Asked if he dances well, a young courtier answers with confidence. At the royal ball, before the King himself, he gets his chance to prove it.

spans.title: The King's Farewell
spans.blurb: An old king, dying in state, calls his court to his bedside: cardinals, princes, weeping duchesses, and at last a small child who will inherit everything.

spans.title: The Affair of the Necklace
spans.blurb: A jeweller arrives at a lady's country house demanding payment for a fabulous necklace the Queen insists she never bought. Someone is lying, and the sums are ruinous.

spans.title: The Concert of Monsieur Vaussore
spans.blurb: A penniless young wanderer reinvents himself as a Parisian music master, though he cannot read a note. Then a professor asks him to compose a piece for his concert.

spans.title: The Examination at Surgeons' Hall
spans.blurb: A trembling young Scot faces a dozen grim examiners for his surgeon's licence, fielding trick questions until his judges start quarrelling among themselves.

spans.title: The Great Fire
spans.blurb: Woken at three in the morning by a maid's report of a fire, a London official goes back to sleep. By daylight, the whole riverfront is burning.

spans.title: Waiting for the Overt Act
spans.blurb: February 1917: a cabinet secretary writes a friend in confidence, recording what the President says behind closed doors as German submarines push a neutral nation toward war.

spans.title: Milk for the Pussens
spans.blurb: A gentle man moves softly about his kitchen at breakfast time, sizing up his black cat as she sizes up him.

spans.title: Tea and Metempsychosis
spans.blurb: He carries the breakfast tray up to his wife, answers her question about a strange word, and tries not to think about the letter under her pillow.

books.pairNote: Adjacent slices of the same Dublin morning, but they share no text and each has its own payoff.

spans.title: The Price of the Colt
spans.blurb: A boy of eight wants a neighbour's colt so badly that his father finally lets him ride over and bargain for it himself.

spans.title: First Day Under Fire
spans.blurb: A young lieutenant advances through tall prairie grass into his first battle, watching cannon balls ricochet slowly enough to dodge, and learning what war actually does.

spans.title: A Distant View of Wilsonople
spans.blurb: A complacent General opens a letter from Italy and finds it composed of ink sketches of a city called Wilsonople. Page by page, they grow alarmingly personal.
